findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
Read the key exported activities. LinkActivity validates its input; WidgetAuthenticationActivity requires device auth. But ShareActivity lets any app silently fire a 'mobile_app.share' event with attacker text to the user's server (it can trigger automations), and AssistActivity, exported without a permission, shows over the keyguard and takes server/pipeline from extras. Whether these are intended capabilities is a product decision. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0365: Exported And Unprotected Services That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
Wearable listeners (WearOnboardingListener, WearDnsRequestListener, PhoneSettingsListener) are only delivered by Play services from paired nodes, and HaCarAppService uses a HostValidator allowlist in release. MatterCommissioningService returns its binder to any caller and relies on unverified GMS-side signature checks (per the manifest comment), which can't be confirmed from code. Ward's analyzer said: Exported services without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0366: Exported And Unprotected Broadcast Receivers That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
TemplateWidget is exported only to get boot broadcasts, yet its onReceive accepts ACTION_APPWIDGET_CREATED from any caller and writes an attacker-supplied serialized TemplateWidgetEntity (a template the server renders with the user's token) into the DB for any widget id. Ward's analyzer said: Exported receivers without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0326: References to APIs Allowing Fallback to Non-Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
The app lock and authenticated widget/notification actions (which can control the home) use BiometricPrompt with DEVICE_CREDENTIAL allowed alongside BIOMETRIC_WEAK.
app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/authenticator/Authenticator.kt:17: Allowed authenticators include device credential fallback and weak biometrics.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
App lock and authenticated widget actions rely only on onAuthenticationSucceeded: authenticate() is called without a CryptoObject, and no key is created with setUserAuthenticationRequired.
app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/authenticator/Authenticator.kt:52: Event-bound BiometricPrompt call without a CryptoObject.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0329: References to APIs Enforcing Authentication without Explicit User Action
findings.explanation:
setConfirmationRequired(false) is used for the single Authenticator that gates the app lock and 'require authentication' widget/notification actions (e.g. door controls), which are sensitive operations needing explicit authorization.
app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/authenticator/Authenticator.kt:48: Passive biometrics accepted without explicit user confirmation.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0337: References to Object Deserialization of Untrusted Data
findings.explanation:
The exported TemplateWidget receiver deserializes a Serializable from extras supplied by any app. Below API 33, BundleCompat.getSerializable deserializes before the type check, so there is no class filtering.
app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/widgets/template/TemplateWidget.kt:110: Serializable read from an externally reachable intent.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0304: References to Sensitive Data Unencrypted via Android Room Database
findings.explanation:
The Room database is built without encryption (no SQLCipher/openHelperFactory) and stores the server access/refresh tokens and saved HTTP basic-auth usernames/passwords in plaintext columns.

common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/database/server/ServerSessionInfo.kt:12: Refresh token stored as plaintext column.
common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/database/authentication/Authentication.kt:16: HTTP basic-auth password stored as plaintext column.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
A custom X509ExtendedTrustManager is installed in OkHttp that, when platform validation fails, retries against a trust manager built from user-installed CAs. This explicitly loosens trust and duplicates what the NSC already allows.
common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/data/CompositeX509ExtendedTrustManager.kt:46: Rejected server chains are retried against the user-CA fallback.
common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/data/TLSHelper.kt:77: User-installed CA trust manager wired into the handshake.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0285: Outdated Android Version Allowing Trust in User-Provided CAs
findings.explanation:
The network security config trusts user-installed CAs outside debug-overrides, so anyone who can install a certificate on the device can read the app's TLS traffic.
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:10: base-config trusts user-installed CAs
